content.title: About
content.content: Soft multigrain pretzels (3048) are tender yet slightly crunchy snacks made from a blend of wheat, rye, oat and barley. They have a mild sweet flavor, a lightly salted crust and a soft interior. Pretzels are suitable as a quick bite or as an addition to salads, soups, or cheese platters.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soft pretzels originated in Germany in the 19th century as a milder alternative to traditional hard pretzels.
The multigrain mix boosts fiber content and makes the product more nutritious.
The classic “knot” shape symbolizes connection and friendship in German culture.
Pretzels are often served with mustard or cheese dips.
In some countries they are used as a base for open‑face sandwiches.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: The grain blend provides a high amount of fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Grains supply thiamine, niacin and folate, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The combination of grains helps maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Pretzels offer a modest amount of protein useful for tissue repair.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: They contain magnesium, iron and zinc, essential for nervous and immune function.

items.title: Grain allergy
items.content: People allergic to wheat, rye or barley should avoid these pretzels.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some varieties are salted; individuals with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While softer pretzels are less calorie‑dense than some snacks, they should still be eaten in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pretzels can be enjoyed straight from the pack, added to salads, used in sandwiches, or served with dips (mustard, cheese, yogurt). They also work well cut into bite‑size pieces for canapés.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life store in the refrigerator to retain softness and prevent drying out. Discard if pretzels become hard, moldy, or develop an off‑odor.
